title: Defining Done for CSLib: What Would a Complete Formally Verified Undergraduate CS Curriculum Look Like?

original_idea.body:
# Defining Done for CSLib: What Would a Complete Formally Verified Undergraduate CS Curriculum Look Like?

**Problem:** CSLib aims to cover undergraduate algorithms and data structures by 2026. The definition of 'complete' (how many algorithms, which edge cases, which security-relevant variants) is underspecified.

**Direction:** Survey 5 undergraduate CS curricula. Extract the complete list of algorithms and data structures taught. Compare against current CSLib coverage. Define a precise specification of 'complete CSLib' including security-relevant variants. Measure current coverage percentage as a baseline.

**Why it matters:** A precise definition of completion enables tracking CSLib progress and identifies whether AI assistance can accelerate the timeline. Without a definition, 'complete CSLib' is not a measurable goal.

**Relevant context:** CSLib paper (arXiv 2602.04846) describes 2026 roadmap at a high level. No precise specification of what constitutes undergraduate-level coverage exists. This is foundational planning work.
